interest: This file is interesting to historians of the Second Sino-Japanese War and East Asian financial history because it highlights the operational survival strategies and jurisdictional maneuvering of Japanese state-chartered banks (the Yokohama Specie Bank and the Bank of Chosen) in China. The 1937 entries illustrate how Japanese banks turned to a neutral American businessman to protect their physical assets during the emergency evacuation of Tsingtao, revealing informal reliance on Western third-party nationals amid escalating warfare. Furthermore, the 1939 entry documents how the Yokohama Specie Bank navigated divided administrative authority in Tientsin by opening a branch in the Japanese concession while retaining its primary office within the foreign-administered British concession.
overview: This file consists of a single Department of State List of Papers docket sheet (Form DS-46), dated October 12, 1945, for decimal file 894.51693, 'Establishment of Japanese Bank in China' (File 318). The docket indexes three communications dating from 1937 and 1939 concerning Japanese financial institutions in China during the Second Sino-Japanese War. The first two entries reference August 1937 telegrams reporting on the Japanese evacuation of Tsingtao (Qingdao), noting that the Yokohama Specie Bank and the Bank of Chosen arranged for a local American businessman to look after their property. The third entry records a January 1939 telegram from the American Consulate General in Tientsin (Tianjin) reporting that the Yokohama Specie Bank had opened a branch in the Japanese concession while temporarily retaining its main office in the British concession.

subfiles.about: A Department of State list of papers indexing records concerning Japanese branch banks and their properties in China during the Sino-Japanese conflict.
subfiles.summary: This document is a Department of State List of Papers (Form DS-46) dated October 12, 1945, cataloguing records under decimal file 894.51693 regarding the establishment and operations of Japanese banks in China. It indexes an August 29, 1937 telegram from Consul Samuel Sokobin in Tsingtao reporting that the Yokohama Specie Bank and the Bank of Chosen asked a local American businessman to safeguard their property during the Japanese evacuation, as well as a related Department telegram of August 30, 1937. It also records a January 6, 1939 telegram from Consul General John K. Caldwell in Tientsin reporting that the Yokohama Specie Bank opened a branch in the Japanese concession while retaining its main office in the British concession.
subfiles.title: Department of State List of Papers: Establishment of Japanese Bank in China
